subject: sst
prompt_en: A crop calendar shows a rice bar from June to October and a wheat bar from November to April on the same field. Describe it in words. Can one farmer grow both on that field in a year?
prompt_hi: Ek crop calendar mein ek hi khet ke liye June se October tak chaawal ki patti aur November se April tak gehun ki patti dikhti hai. Ise shabdon mein batao. Kya ek kisaan saal mein us khet par dono uga sakta hai?
answer: Rice is grown in the kharif season from June to October, then wheat in the rabi season from November to April; yes, the farmer can grow both one after the other on the same field in one year (a rice–wheat rotation), as is common in Punjab and Haryana.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Which crops grow in or near your district or state, and in which season? Name one challenge farmers there face. (If you live in a city, trace where the wheat in your roti or the rice on your plate comes from.)
prompt_hi: Tumhare zile ya rajya mein ya uske aas-paas kaunsi fasalein ugti hain, aur kis mausam mein? Wahan ke kisaanon ki ek mushkil batao. (Agar shehar mein rehte ho, toh pata karo ki tumhari roti ka gehun ya thaali ka chaawal kahan se aata hai.)
answer: A good answer names real local crops with correct seasons (e.g. Punjab: rice in kharif, wheat in rabi; Maharashtra: cotton and soybean in kharif; Bihar: rice and wheat) and a fitting challenge (falling groundwater, late monsoon, small fields, low prices); city children trace a plausible source region.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend the story of Indian farming in five steps, from Mehrgarh to today, including one problem and one solution.
prompt_hi: Dost ko Bharatiya kheti ki kahaani paanch steps mein samjhao, Mehrgarh se aaj tak, ek samasya aur ek samaadhaan ke saath.
answer: Key idea: early farming at Mehrgarh (c. 7000 BCE) → Harappan farming with wheat, barley, cotton → ancient irrigation such as tanks, stepwells and the Kallanai → the Green Revolution (1960s) bringing food self-sufficiency → today's problems (e.g. falling groundwater) and solutions (e.g. drip irrigation, millets).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Using a map, say in which direction each lies from India: Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Myanmar, Bhutan, the Maldives.
prompt_hi: Map dekh ke batao ki har desh Bharat se kis disha mein hai: Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Myanmar, Bhutan, Maldives.
answer: Nepal – north; Bangladesh – east; Sri Lanka – south (south-east of the tip); Pakistan – west/north-west; Myanmar – east; Bhutan – north-east; Maldives – south-west.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name India's two island neighbours, and the narrow stretch of sea between India and Sri Lanka.
prompt_hi: Bharat ke do dweep padosi desh aur Bharat-Sri Lanka ke beech ke sankare samudri hisse ka naam batao.
answer: Sri Lanka and the Maldives; the Palk Strait.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Trace the journey of the Brahmaputra from its source to the sea, naming the countries and two of its other names.
prompt_hi: Brahmaputra ka safar uske udgam se samundar tak batao, deshon ke naam aur uske do aur naam bhi.
answer: It begins in Tibet (China) as the Yarlung Tsangpo, enters India in Arunachal Pradesh (as the Siang/Dihang), flows through Assam as the Brahmaputra, enters Bangladesh (as the Jamuna), joins the Ganga's waters and reaches the Bay of Bengal.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do India and its neighbours need to cooperate over rivers?
prompt_hi: Bharat aur uske padosiyon ko nadiyon ke maamle mein sahyog kyun karna padta hai?
answer: Rivers cross borders, so what happens upstream (dams, water use, pollution, heavy rain) affects people downstream; countries must share water fairly, share flood warnings and data, and manage rivers together.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Very heavy rain falls in Tibet and Arunachal Pradesh for a week. Predict what might happen downstream in Assam and Bangladesh.
prompt_hi: Tibet aur Arunachal Pradesh mein ek hafte tak bahut bhaari baarish hoti hai. Socho neeche ki taraf Assam aur Bangladesh mein kya ho sakta hai.
answer: The Brahmaputra will swell and carry much more water downstream, so Assam and later Bangladesh may face floods; early warnings shared between countries can help people prepare.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Give two cultural links between India and its neighbours.
prompt_hi: Bharat aur uske padosiyon ke beech do saanskritik rishte batao.
answer: For example: Buddhism links Lumbini in Nepal (the Buddha's birthplace) and Bodh Gaya in India and is followed in Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Myanmar; Bengali is spoken in West Bengal and Bangladesh; Punjabi on both sides of the India–Pakistan border; Tagore wrote the national anthems of India and Bangladesh; shared foods, festivals and cricket.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare Nepal and Bangladesh: the main landform, a major river, and the main language.
prompt_hi: Nepal aur Bangladesh ki tulna karo: mukhya bhoo-roop, ek badi nadi, aur mukhya bhasha.
answer: Nepal: mostly mountains and hills of the Himalayas, with Mount Everest; rivers like the Koshi and Gandaki flowing down to India; Nepali. Bangladesh: low, flat delta land; the Padma (Ganga), Jamuna (Brahmaputra) and Meghna; Bengali (Bangla).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why are Lumbini in Nepal and Bodh Gaya in India both important to Buddhists, and what does this show about the two countries?
prompt_hi: Nepal ka Lumbini aur Bharat ka Bodh Gaya dono Buddh dharm ke maanne waalon ke liye kyun mahatvapoorn hain, aur isse dono deshon ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Lumbini is where the Buddha was born and Bodh Gaya is where he attained enlightenment; this shared heritage links Nepal and India and draws pilgrims from across Asia to both.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Give three reasons why good relations with neighbours are useful for India.
prompt_hi: 3 kaaran batao ki padosiyon se achhe rishte Bharat ke liye kyun faydemand hain.
answer: Trade and transport (goods, roads, railways, ports); sharing rivers and flood warnings; helping each other in disasters (such as the 2004 tsunami or the 2015 Nepal earthquake); tourism and pilgrimage; peace and security along borders.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistakes: "Sri Lanka is north of India, and Bangladesh is on India's west."
prompt_hi: Galtiyaan pakdo: "Sri Lanka Bharat ke uttar mein hai, aur Bangladesh Bharat ke pashchim mein."
answer: Sri Lanka lies to the south of India, across the Palk Strait; Bangladesh lies to the east, surrounded on most sides by Indian states such as West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find one thing in your own life connected to a neighbouring country — a food, a festival, a song, a sport, a product, or a family story. Explain the link.
prompt_hi: Apni zindagi mein kisi padosi desh se judi ek cheez dhoondho — khaana, tyohaar, gaana, khel, koi saamaan, ya parivaar ki koi kahaani. Rishta samjhao.
answer: A good answer names a real link and explains it (e.g. momos came through Tibetan and Nepali communities; India–Pakistan, India–Sri Lanka and India–Bangladesh cricket matches; Bengali songs and Tagore; Buddhist monasteries; relatives across a border).

subject: sst
prompt_en: What is SAARC, when was it formed, and how many members does it have?
prompt_hi: SAARC kya hai, kab bana, aur iske kitne sadasya hain?
answer: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, formed in 1985, with eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend how India is linked to its neighbours by land, by rivers and by culture. Give one example of each.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki Bharat apne padosiyon se zameen, nadiyon aur sanskriti ke zariye kaise juda hai. Har ek ka ek example do.
answer: Key idea: by land — shared borders and the Himalayas with Nepal, Bhutan and China; by rivers — the Brahmaputra and Ganga flow on into Bangladesh, the Indus into Pakistan; by culture — Buddhism, shared languages like Bengali and Punjabi, Tagore's anthems, food and cricket.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name the century for each: Harsha's reign (606–647 CE); the Kailasa temple at Ellora (built in the 700s CE); Rajaraja Chola's temple at Thanjavur (completed around 1010 CE).
prompt_hi: Har ek ki shatabdi batao: Harsha ka shaasan (606–647 CE); Ellora ka Kailasa mandir (700s CE mein bana); Thanjavur mein Rajaraja Chola ka mandir (lagbhag 1010 CE mein poora hua).
answer: Harsha – 7th century CE; Kailasa temple – 8th century CE; Thanjavur temple – 11th century CE.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Using a map, describe in words where these kingdoms were centred: Harsha, the Chalukyas of Badami, the Pallavas, the Rashtrakutas, the Palas.
prompt_hi: Map dekh ke shabdon mein batao ki yeh rajya kahan kendrit the: Harsha, Badami ke Chalukya, Pallava, Rashtrakuta, Pala.
answer: Harsha – Kanauj in the Ganga plains (Uttar Pradesh); Chalukyas – Badami in northern Karnataka (Deccan); Pallavas – Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu; Rashtrakutas – the western Deccan (Maharashtra–Karnataka, with Ellora in Maharashtra); Palas – Bengal and Bihar in the east.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Who stopped Harsha from expanding into the Deccan, near which river, and which inscription records it?
prompt_hi: Harsha ko Deccan mein failne se kisne roka, kis nadi ke paas, aur kaunsa shilalekh iska ullekh karta hai?
answer: The Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, near the Narmada river; the Aihole inscription (634 CE), written by his court poet Ravikirti.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why did the Palas, the Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas all fight to control Kanauj?
prompt_hi: Pala, Pratihara aur Rashtrakuta — teenon Kanauj par kabza karne ke liye kyun lade?
answer: Kanauj lay in the rich, fertile Ganga plains and on important trade routes, and as Harsha's former capital it carried great prestige — controlling it was a sign of being the most powerful ruler in north India.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the Pallavas and the Chalukyas of Badami: their capitals, one famous monument each, and how they were linked.
prompt_hi: Pallava aur Badami ke Chalukya ki tulna karo: unki rajdhaniyaan, har ek ka ek prasiddh smarak, aur dono ka aapas mein rishta.
answer: Pallavas: capital Kanchipuram; monuments such as the rathas and Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram. Chalukyas: capital Badami (Vatapi); temples at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal. They were rivals who fought repeatedly — the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I captured Vatapi around 642 CE — yet both were great temple builders.

subject: sst
prompt_en: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved from a single rock, working from the top down. What does this tell us about its builders?
prompt_hi: Ellora ka Kailasa mandir ek hi chattaan ko oopar se neeche kaat kar banaya gaya. Isse iske banaane waalon ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: They had excellent planning, engineering and carving skill — they had to imagine the whole temple inside the rock before starting, since mistakes could not be fixed by adding stone — and the Rashtrakuta rulers had the wealth and organisation to support huge numbers of workers for many years.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistakes: "The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built by the Rashtrakutas in Bengal."
prompt_hi: Galtiyaan pakdo: "Mahabalipuram ka Shore Temple Bengal mein Rashtrakutas ne banaya tha."
answer: The Shore Temple was built by the Pallavas (around the early 8th century), and Mahabalipuram is on the Tamil Nadu coast near Chennai, not in Bengal.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name two contributions of the Pala kings to learning.
prompt_hi: Pala rajaon ke shiksha mein do yogdaan batao.
answer: They supported the great university at Nalanda and founded Vikramashila (under Dharmapala), centres of Buddhist learning that attracted students from Tibet and other parts of Asia.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Xuanzang wrote very warmly about Harsha. Why is his account useful, and why must historians be careful with it?
prompt_hi: Xuanzang ne Harsha ke baare mein bahut taareef karte hue likha. Unka vivaran kyun upyogi hai, aur itihaaskaron ko saavdhaan kyun rehna chahiye?
answer: Useful: he was an eyewitness who described cities, Nalanda, festivals and Harsha's court. Careful: Harsha was his host and patron, so he may have praised him; as a Buddhist pilgrim he focused on Buddhist matters; as a foreigner he might have misunderstood some things. Historians check his account against inscriptions and Indian texts.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if Pulakeshin II had not stopped Harsha at the Narmada, what might have changed? Why can historians not be sure?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar Pulakeshin II ne Harsha ko Narmada par na roka hota, toh kya badal sakta tha? Itihaaskar iske baare mein pakka kyun nahi keh sakte?
answer: Harsha might have extended his rule into the Deccan, creating a larger kingdom across north and central India, and the Chalukyas might not have become a great power. But this is a "what if" — we have no evidence of events that did not happen, so historians can only reason about possibilities.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the Nagara (northern) and Dravida (southern) temple styles.
prompt_hi: Nagara (uttari) aur Dravida (dakshini) mandir shailiyon ki tulna karo.
answer: Nagara: a tall, curved tower (shikhara) rising over the sanctum, common in north India. Dravida: a pyramid-shaped tower (vimana) rising in storeys, often within a walled courtyard with gateways, common in south India. Pattadakal in Karnataka has temples in both styles side by side.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find an old temple, fort, stupa, mosque or other monument in or near your state. Who built it, roughly when, and what does it tell us about the people of that time?
prompt_hi: Apne rajya mein ya uske paas koi puraana mandir, kila, stoop, masjid ya aur koi smarak dhoondho. Use kisne banaya, lagbhag kab, aur woh us samay ke logon ke baare mein kya batata hai?
answer: A good answer names a real monument, a plausible builder and period, and draws one sound inference (e.g. skill, wealth, beliefs, trade or defence needs of the time).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend that India in the 6th–10th centuries had many powerful kingdoms at the same time. Give three kingdoms, their regions and one achievement each.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki 6vi se 10vi shatabdi tak Bharat mein ek saath kai shaktishaali rajya the. 3 rajya, unke kshetra aur har ek ki ek uplabdhi batao.
answer: Key idea: many kingdoms coexisted and competed — e.g. Harsha (Kanauj, north; patron of learning, Xuanzang's visit), Pallavas (Kanchipuram, south; Mahabalipuram temples), Rashtrakutas (Deccan; Kailasa temple at Ellora), Palas (Bengal–Bihar; Nalanda and Vikramashila).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why could the Chola king Rajendra I send a navy all the way to Southeast Asia, and why did he want to?
prompt_hi: Chola raja Rajendra I apni nausena Dakshin-Poorv Asia tak kyun bhej paaye, aur ve aisa kyun karna chahte the?
answer: The Cholas controlled ports on the Coromandel coast and had a strong navy and experienced sailors; they wanted to protect and control the rich sea trade routes to Southeast Asia and China, which were being blocked or taxed by the Srivijaya kingdom.

subject: sst
prompt_en: On a map of Chola power, describe in words how far their campaigns and influence reached from their home in Tamil Nadu.
prompt_hi: Chola shakti ke map ko dekh ke shabdon mein batao ki Tamil Nadu ke apne ghar se unke abhiyaan aur prabhaav kahan tak pahunche.
answer: From the Kaveri delta in Tamil Nadu they controlled much of south India, conquered northern Sri Lanka, reached the Maldives, marched north as far as the Ganga in Bengal, and sent a naval expedition across the Bay of Bengal to Southeast Asia (the Malay peninsula and Sumatra).

subject: sst
prompt_en: How were members of the village assembly at Uttaramerur chosen?
prompt_hi: Uttaramerur mein gaon ki sabha ke sadasya kaise chune jaate the?
answer: Qualified candidates' names were written on palm-leaf tickets and put in a pot; a young child drew out the tickets, and those drawn became members — the kudavolai (pot-ticket) system. Rules also barred people who had not given proper accounts.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the Chola village assembly at Uttaramerur with a gram panchayat today: how members are chosen and what both have in common.
prompt_hi: Uttaramerur ki Chola gram sabha ki tulna aaj ki gram panchayat se karo: sadasya kaise chune jaate hain aur dono mein kya same hai.
answer: Uttaramerur: members drawn by lot (kudavolai) from candidates who met set qualifications. Gram panchayat: members and the sarpanch are elected by villagers' votes. Common: both are forms of local self-government where villages run their own affairs such as water tanks, roads and disputes.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Chola bronzes like Nataraja were made by the lost-wax method. Why is each statue one of a kind?
prompt_hi: Nataraja jaisi Chola kaansya moortiyaan "lost-wax" vidhi se banti thin. Har moorti anokhi kyun hoti hai?
answer: The artist first shapes the figure in wax, covers it in clay, heats it so the wax melts out ("lost"), pours molten metal into the space, and then breaks the clay mould to remove the statue; since both the wax model and the mould are destroyed, each statue is unique.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Put in order: Second Battle of Tarain; Brihadeeswara temple completed; Delhi Sultanate founded; Mahmud raids Somnath; First Battle of Tarain.
prompt_hi: Kram mein lagao: Tarain ka doosra yuddh; Brihadeeswara mandir poora hua; Delhi Sultanate ki sthaapna; Mahmud ka Somnath par hamla; Tarain ka pehla yuddh.
answer: Brihadeeswara completed (c. 1010) → Mahmud raids Somnath (1025–26) → First Battle of Tarain (1191) → Second Battle of Tarain (1192) → Delhi Sultanate founded (1206).

subject: sst
prompt_en: What happened at Tarain in 1191 and in 1192?
prompt_hi: 1191 aur 1192 mein Tarain mein kya hua?
answer: 1191: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori (First Battle of Tarain). 1192: Ghori returned and defeated Prithviraj (Second Battle of Tarain), opening the way for rule from Delhi.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What were Mahmud of Ghazni's raids mainly aimed at, and did he set up rule over most of India?
prompt_hi: Ghazni ke Mahmud ke hamle mukhya roop se kis cheez ke liye the, aur kya usne Bharat ke zyaadatar hisse par raaj kiya?
answer: They were mainly aimed at seizing wealth — rich temples and cities stored gold, jewels and treasure — which he carried back to Ghazni to strengthen his kingdom in Afghanistan. He did not rule most of India; he annexed only parts of the north-west such as Punjab.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Al-Biruni came to India with Mahmud's court but wrote a careful book about India. Why is his book valuable, and what should historians keep in mind?
prompt_hi: Al-Biruni Mahmud ke darbaar ke saath Bharat aaye par unhone Bharat par ek dhyaan se likhi kitaab likhi. Unki kitaab kyun mulyavaan hai, aur itihaaskaron ko kya dhyaan rakhna chahiye?
answer: Valuable: he learned Sanskrit and studied Indian mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, customs and geography in detail, so it is a rich record of the time. Keep in mind: he was an outsider writing for readers in his own lands, with his own views and comparisons, so his judgements are compared with Indian sources.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistake: "In the 11th and 12th centuries nothing was built or created in India because of the invasions."
prompt_hi: Galti pakdo: "11vi aur 12vi shatabdi mein hamlon ki wajah se Bharat mein kuch bhi nahi bana ya racha gaya."
answer: Much was built and created: the Brihadeeswara temple and Chola bronzes in the south, the Khajuraho temples of the Chandelas, the Modhera Sun temple of the Solankis, Hoysala temples at Belur and Halebidu, and Raja Bhoja's works in Malwa.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the south and the north-west of India in the 11th century: what was happening in each?
prompt_hi: 11vi shatabdi mein Bharat ke dakshin aur uttar-pashchim ki tulna karo: dono jagah kya ho raha tha?
answer: South: the Cholas were a strong, expanding power with a navy, great temples, bronzes and overseas trade. North-west and north: many kingdoms were divided and faced repeated raids by Mahmud of Ghazni; later, in the 12th century, Ghori's campaigns led to the Delhi Sultanate.
